title: Stop Using Your Handbrake Like This (Part 1)

script.narration: Stop using your handbrake wrong. Many think pulling it up hard is the only way to park safely, but that is a myth. The reality is that the ratcheting mechanism can wear out prematurely if you don't engage it properly.
script.visual_search: driver pulling manual handbrake in car

script.narration: To save your cable, press the release button before you pull the lever up. This stops the clicking sound and prevents metal-on-metal wear. Follow so you don't miss Part 2!
script.visual_search: close up of hand pressing parking brake button

description:
Learn the correct way to operate your car's manual handbrake to avoid costly repairs. Many drivers damage their parking brake mechanism by ignoring this simple tip.

Master your vehicle controls and ensure your car stays safely parked every time. Follow for daily driving tips and expert car advice.

quality_problems: fact-check: The claim that pressing the release button before pulling the lever saves the cable or prevents wear is misleading; the ratcheting mechanism is specifically designed to click to ensure the brake is locked in place.; Bypassing the ratchet by holding the button while pulling can cause the brake to fail to lock entirely, creating a safety hazard.; The advice contradicts standard vehicle owner manual operating procedures for manual parking brakes.
